title: build step answer
description: One plan item, built test-first. failedBefore and passedAfter are both const true: there is no shape in this contract for a change whose test did not fail first.

skills.description: Every Superpowers skill invoked in this step. The driver cross-checks this against the Skill calls in the run log, so a claim here the log does not show is a failed step.

task.description: The plan task this answer builds, by its title.

redWhen.description: The production change that makes this test fail — the fix deleted, not a typo introduced. A test whose author cannot name one is measuring the shape of the code.

testCommit.description: The commit that adds the test, and nothing else. The driver re-runs the test itself at the change's parent and requires it to fail, so it needs a commit to read the test out of — failedBefore is the claim, this is what makes it checkable.

implCommit.description: The commit that makes the test pass. It must differ from testCommit: one squashed commit cannot show which came first, which is the thing being prevented.

surfaces.description: Every other place that shows the state this change alters, and what was changed there. A state change that updates one surface of three is the most repeated review send-back.

changelog.description: Either the entry file written, or the reason there is none. Never both, and never neither.

question.description: Why this step cannot finish. Answerable in a line: a yes/no or a pick.

questionKind.description: What kind of question it is. `base-red`: a red that fails the same way at the merge base. `uncommitted-fix`: the change passes but is not committed. `already-fixed`: the ask already holds on the integration branch. `uat-data`: it wants UAT or production data. `other`: anything else. Never ask for UAT or production data: measure on the local seed or the fixtures, and say so in the pull request.

questionFor.description: Who answers the question. `owner`: pixels, a picture, a product or commercial call, or the data model. `pm`: the ticket's shape — which repo, how it splits, the order, the wording of its acceptance. Unsure is `owner`; the driver treats anything but `pm` as the owner's.

testOnly.description: A task whose deliverable IS the test: the code it covers already exists, so nothing can be red before it. The driver plants `break` in the production code at testCommit and requires the test to FAIL, then removes it and requires the test to PASS. Use this instead of testFirst only when the task changes no production code.

testCommit.description: The commit that adds the test. The driver runs the test in a copy of this commit.

break.description: A literal find/replace in the production file the test covers that DELETES the behaviour under test (the death, not a typo). Never the test file itself. `find` must appear in `file` at testCommit.

noCode.description: A task that changes no code and commits nothing (re-run a failed CI job). The driver requires no diff since the task started and reads `run` itself: a workflow run of this repo that concluded success on the branch's current head. A diff, or a run that is missing, not green or on another commit, is refused. Use this instead of testFirst or testOnly only when the task leaves the tree unchanged.

reason.description: Why this task has no code to change.

run.description: The CI run that is this task's evidence: its URL (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>) or its numeric id.

trunkMerge.description: A task whose only commit merges the trunk into the branch. It needs no test pair: the driver requires `commit` to be a merge this task made (one already on the branch when the task started is refused), whose second parent is on the trunk and whose tree is what `git merge` gives, and the task to have committed nothing else. A conflict resolved by hand is accepted when no marker remains, only the conflicted files differ from the clean merge, and the project's gates pass on the merge; any other edit is a change and is refused here.

replacedTests.description: Every test file in which this step removed, reworded or skipped an it()/test() case. `file` is the repo-relative path exactly as git shows it. Give exactly one of `coveredBy` — a bare repo-relative path, nothing else, to the test file at head that now pins the same behaviour (the same file, for a reworded case) — or `removedBecause`, one line on why the behaviour is gone. The ship step writes these into the pull request's `## Deleted tests` section, and the deleted-tests gate checks each line. Empty when no case was removed, reworded or skipped.

gitActions.description: Git steps your permission mode refuses, which the driver checks and runs after this answer, in order: commitMerge stages the resolved conflicted paths and finishes the merge in progress with --no-edit; resetTo moves the branch to sha, one of its own commits not on the trunk or its head on origin; dropLocalCommits resets the branch to origin when every local commit is already there. One refused stops the rest.
